overview: File combines a 1938 despatch finding Japan had no government hospitals treating foreign seamen, and an unrelated 1930 memo praising a Japanese-press study for limited circulation to correspondents.

people.role: Correspondent to whom the report on the Japanese press might be shown

people.name: RSM (unidentified)
people.role: Division of Far Eastern Affairs official who initialed or drafted the memorandum

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch 1138 from Yokohama
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects readers to a medical-relief file containing Johansen’s October 15, 1938 despatch on the treatment of sick and disabled seamen by foreign governments.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a 1938 Yokohama despatch concerns medical relief for sick foreign seamen in Japan.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1138 on medical services for foreign seamen in Japan
subfiles.from: Berge R. Johansen, American Vice Consul
subfiles.about: Johansen reports the result of an inquiry into Japanese government medical provision for sick and disabled seamen from foreign vessels.
subfiles.summary: Johansen reports Japan has no government hospitals providing medical care to sick foreign seamen.

subfiles.title: Division memorandum assessing a report on “The Japanese Press”
subfiles.from: U.S. Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs (initialed RSM)
subfiles.about: An internal memorandum evaluates a comprehensive report on the history, organization, ethics, and influence of the Japanese press.
subfiles.summary: Memo praises a Japanese-press study, approving limited circulation to a trusted correspondent.

interest: Shows Japan lacked government hospitals for foreign seamen, alongside an unrelated 1930 press-report memo.
